# Pin HashHistory: one route stack per browser window

## Welcome 👋

Neo apps route by the URL hash, and Neo can run one app across several browser windows. `Neo.util.HashHistory` remembers the recent routes: one stack per window, newest first. It is about sixty lines of plain logic with no test, which makes it a good first spec.

This is a **good first issue** for Hacktoberfest 2026. It needs Node.js and a clone of this repository: no Docker, no AI setup.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Reserved for first-time Neo.mjs contributors.** The maintainer team will not claim, edit, or implement this issue through **2026-10-31**. Comment here to claim it, and ask anything on this issue.

**Set up once:** follow [Set up the engine from a clone](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/CONTRIBUTING.md#set-up-the-engine-from-a-clone), including `npm run bundle-browser-deps`: without it the unit suite selects zero tests.

## Where things live

- Source: `src/util/HashHistory.mjs`, a singleton with `push(data)`, `first()`, `second()`, `getAt()`, `getCount()`, `getStack()` and a `change` event
- New test file: `test/playwright/unit/util/HashHistory.spec.mjs`
- Pattern to copy: `test/playwright/unit/util/Array.spec.mjs` (the `setup()` call and imports)
- Tip: it is a singleton, so its stacks survive from one test to the next. Start each test with `HashHistory.stacks = {}`.

## What to cover

| Action | Expected |
|---|---|
| `push({hashString: 'a', windowId: 'w1'})`, then `'b'` | `first('w1')` is the `'b'` entry, `second('w1')` the `'a'` entry |
| the same `hashString` twice in a row | stored once, and no second `change` event |
| `change` event | fires with `(newEntry, previousEntry)`, and `previousEntry` is `null` on the first push |
| pushes for `'w1'` and `'w2'` | two independent stacks: `getCount('w1')` counts only its own |
| 51 different pushes (`maxItems` is 50) | the oldest entry is dropped, and the count stays 50 |
| `getAt(0, 'w1')` | the newest entry |
| a read with no `windowId` | the first window's stack |

**Something to look at while you are in there:** `push()` runs `delete data[windowId]`. That deletes a property *named after the window id's value* (for example `data['w1']`), not the `windowId` property itself. Pin what the code does today. If you think it meant `delete data.windowId`, say so on this issue before changing `src/`: that is a behaviour change, and #5492 introduced the line.

## Done when

- [ ] `test/playwright/unit/util/HashHistory.spec.mjs` exists, following the pattern file's setup.
- [ ] One `test(...)` per table row.
- [ ] Test-only, as above.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit -- test/playwright/unit/util/HashHistory.spec.mjs` passes.
- [ ] `npm run test-unit` passes.

## Out of scope

The router and controllers that read the history (`src/controller/Base.mjs`), and browser integration.

## While you wait for review

You just pinned one small piece of a multi-threaded application engine: in Neo.mjs your app's code runs inside a web worker, and the main thread only paints. Two things worth ten minutes:

- **See the part nobody expects.** Run `npm run build-themes -- -n -e dev -t all` and `npm run server-start`, open `apps/workstation/`, and drag a tab out of the browser window. It becomes its own OS window, still running, with the same component instances and the same worker. [Benefits: Introduction](https://github.com/neomjs/neo/blob/dev/learn/benefits/Introduction.md) explains why that is possible.
- **Your coding agent can go much further here.** The skills this repository's AI maintainers work with are published on npm as [`neo-agent-skills`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/neo-agent-skills), and they need no Knowledge Base and no Memory Core. With Claude or GPT beside you, the `help wanted` issues are within reach after this one.

- 2026-11-02T15:54:12Z @tobiu referenced in commit `07339eb` - "test(util): pin Neo.util.HashHistory behavior (#19132) (#20197)

Neo.util.HashHistory keeps one route stack per window and had no test.
The spec pins each row of #19132: first(), second() and getAt(0) order, a
repeated hashString stored once with one change event, the change event's
(newEntry, previousEntry) arguments with null on the first push,
independent per-window stacks, the 50-entry cap dropping the oldest, and a
read without a windowId using the first window's stack.

It also pins what `delete data[windowId]` in push() does today: it deletes
the key named after the window id's value, so stored entries keep their
windowId. controller/Base.mjs initAsync() relies on that
(`currentHash.windowId === windowId`), so the line should not become
`delete data.windowId`.

The singleton keeps its stacks between tests, so each test starts from
`HashHistory.stacks = {}` and removes any change listener it adds."
